## Question 6

```{r}
mean_na <- function(x) {
  mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)}
#to ceeck it we are taking an example 
v <- c(2, 4, NA, 6, 8)
mean_na(v)
```

## Question 7

```{r}
# Create data frame with 6 observations
df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:6,
  age = c(22, 27, 24, 30, 26, 21),
  gender = c("F", "M", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  income = c(20000, 35000, 25000, 40000, 32000, 18000))
#(a) Rename variables
colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "age"] <- "age_years"
colnames(df)[colnames(df) == "income"] <- "annual_income"
#(b) Add indicator variable (age > 25)
df$older_than_25 <- df$age_years > 25
#(c) Subset individuals older than 25
df_sub <- df[df$older_than_25 == TRUE, ]
#(d) Keep only id and indicator variable
final_df <- df_sub[, c("id", "older_than_25")]
final_df
```

## Question 8

```{r}
#Create data frame with four numeric variables
df <- data.frame(
  a = c(2, 4, 6, NA, 8),
  b = c(1, 3, 5, 7, NA),
  c = c(10, 12, NA, 14, 16),
  d = c(5, NA, 9, 11, 13))
#Define function
median_dev_fun <- function(data) {
  
  data$a_md <- data$a - median(data$a, na.rm = TRUE)
  data$b_md <- data$b - median(data$b, na.rm = TRUE)
  data$c_md <- data$c - median(data$c, na.rm = TRUE)
  data$d_md <- data$d - median(data$d, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  data$sum_md <- data$a_md + data$b_md + data$c_md + data$d_md
  
  data
}

#Apply function
result <- median_dev_fun(df)
result
```
